logline: Six Busan high schoolers in 1997 navigate K-pop obsession and first love, their story told in flashback from a 2012 reunion where one couple is about to announce an engagement - but whose?

renewal.note: Reply 1997 was a standalone anthology entry; subsequent Reply series (1994, 1988) share the creative team but feature entirely new casts and settings. The 1997 story concluded with its 16-episode run.

bollymeter.basis: One of the highest-rated cable dramas in Korean television history at broadcast; praised across critics and audiences for period authenticity, the dual-timeline structure's central mystery, and breakout performances by Jung Eun-ji and Seo In-guk. IMDb audience consensus sits at 9.0.

seasons.review_body: Reply 1997 premiered on tvN in July 2012 with minimal promotional fanfare and quickly became a phenomenon driven entirely by word of mouth, breaking the 6-percent ratings threshold considered exceptional for Korean cable at the time. Critics and viewers aligned on the same virtues: the show's laser-sharp recreation of 1990s Busan, its affectionate portrait of K-pop idol fandom, and the dual-timeline structure that sustains a central romantic mystery across all 16 episodes. Jung Eun-ji's lead performance as the irreverent Shi-won and Seo In-guk's restrained counterpoint earned genuine industry recognition. The series established the Reply franchise template and is routinely cited as the entry that proved cable drama could rival the prestige of public broadcast in South Korea. IMDb audience rating of 9.0 confirms lasting affection across international audiences.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Reply 1997 Season 1 Episode 1 aired July 24, 2012 on tvN as the premiere of a 16-episode series that became one of the highest-rated Korean cable dramas in the medium's history, driven almost entirely by word of mouth after breaking the 6-percent threshold. IMDb audience scored the series 9.0. The premiere opens in 2012 at a high-school reunion where one couple is about to announce an engagement - identities withheld - then pulls back to 1997 Busan where Shi-won and her K-pop obsession establish the show's tonal register immediately. Director Shin Won-ho's structural hook is embedded in the first twenty minutes with casual confidence, posing the question that will sustain 16 episodes before the audience has met the characters in their full context. Jung Eun-ji's Shi-won announces itself as a defining comedic-dramatic performance in K-drama's cable era.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere opens in 2012 at a high-school reunion, immediately planting the question of which couple is engaged, then pulls back to 1997 Busan to introduce Shi-won and her orbit. The show's dual-timeline hook is established in the first twenty minutes with casual confidence.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The 2012 reunion scene that withholds the answer the rest of the series is structured to deliver - the mystery is posed before the audience has even met the characters.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.review_body: Reply 1997 Season 1 Episode 16 aired September 18, 2012 on tvN as the finale of the 16-episode series that broke Korean cable's 6-percent threshold and earned an IMDb audience score of 9.0. The series' word-of-mouth reputation was built on the promise this episode delivered. The finale resolves the central mystery of who ends up with whom - a question the show has actively misdirected across 15 episodes using both characters' relationship dynamics and the structural ambiguity of the 2012 reunion framing - and delivers the revelation with emotional precision calibrated to the characters' histories rather than to audience preference for one pairing over another. The reveal's quiet execution, choosing understatement over announcement, was cited by Korean audiences and international viewers alike as the benchmark of how the Reply franchise understood the relationship between structure and emotional payoff.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the central mystery of who ends up with whom, a question the show has cultivated and misdirected across 15 episodes. The reveal lands with emotional precision because the series has done the work of making the audience genuinely uncertain - not through gimmickry but through honest character writing.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The engagement reveal - who it is, and the quiet way the show chose to tell us, is the conversation Reply 1997 fans still have.
